chunks: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, told me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told me, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i the Judge, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Iblis came to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him) while he was conversing with his Lord, and an Angel from the Angels said to him: What do you seek from him while he is in this condition, conversing with his Lord? He said: I seek from him what I sought from his father, Adam, when he was in the Garden.

Among what He conversed to him was that He said to him: O Musa, I do not accept the prayer except for he who humbled to My Greatness, constrained his heart to fear Me, covered his day with My remembrance, did not settle a night whilst insisting on intentional mistake, and knew the truth of My Allies and Beloved.

Then he said: O Lord, do you mean by Your Beloved and Allies, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qoub? He said: They are as such, O Musa, however, I intended he because of whom I created Adam and Hawwa', and he because of whom I created Paradise and the Fire.
Then Musa said: And who is he, O Lord? He said: Muhammad, Ahmad, I derived his name from My Name, because I am the Praised.

Then Musa said: O Lord, make me among his nation. He said: You are, O Musa, from his nation if you know him, know his rank and the rank of his Household. Indeed, the example of him and the example of his Household and that which I have created, is like the example of Firdaus in the Gardens, whose trees never dry, nor does its taste change.

Hence, those who know them and know their truth, I will make for him at the occasion of ignorance, forbearance, and at the occasion of darkness, a light, and I will respond to him before he calls unto Me and I will give him before he asks Me. The narration is long, we took from it the place of need.
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Beloved' for whom God created Paradise and Hell according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the theological centrality of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and his Ahl al-Bayt as the ultimate purpose of creation, linking their recognition directly to the acceptance of worship. The text emphasizes that true devotion requires not just ritual prayer but a profound love for the Imams, who are compared to the eternal Paradise, ensuring divine responsiveness even before supplication is made. This underscores the Shia doctrine of *Wilayah* as the essential key to spiritual success and divine grace.
